one_liner: Pure-safe-Rust PNG/APNG decoder and encoder that decodes faster than libpng on most images; Chromium's default PNG decoder.
what_it_does: The `png` crate decodes and encodes PNG and APNG in safe Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). The decoder is a builder (`Decoder::new(BufRead + Seek)`, `read_info()`, `next_frame(&mut buf)` or `read_row()`) into a caller-allocated buffer, with a small set of libpng-like transforms (EXPAND, STRIP_16, ALPHA); a `StreamingDecoder` supports progressive decoding of partial data. It is not an API drop-in for libpng and has no C ABI of its own.
how_it_is_fast: Since 0.17.8 (after the Wuffs measurement) decompression always uses fdeflate, a custom safe DEFLATE decoder, and the zlib Adler-32 check is skipped by default while chunk CRC32 is still verified (crc32fast, simd-adler32 when checking). Unfiltering is written as component-wise unrolled byte-array loops that LLVM auto-vectorizes (src/filter/optimization-notes.md, PR #382), with explicit `std::simd` Paeth paths only behind the nightly `unstable` feature. 0.18 unfilters in place and shrinks internal buffers so data stays in cache between inflate and unfilter (image-rs blog, 2026-06-18).
when_to_use: Rust or mixed Rust/C++ codebases that decode untrusted PNG/APNG and want memory safety without giving up speed (it is Chromium's default PNG decoder since M139 and backs GNOME's glycin).
Throughput-bound batch decoding of typical web/screenshot/photo PNGs: the maintainers' QOI-corpus run (2,848 images) reports 339.9 vs 180.4 MP/s geomean against libpng+zlib-ng on a Ryzen 9 7950X.
APNG decoding or encoding, which upstream libpng does not support.
Fast lossless PNG writing where a lighter compression ratio is acceptable: the fdeflate-based fast mode (fpnge-inspired) trades ratio for an order-of-magnitude encode speedup per the blog.
when_not_to_use: Plain C++ projects that cannot add a Rust toolchain and an FFI layer: the crate exposes only a Rust API (Chromium wrote its own integration).

Android/ARM64 latency-sensitive decoding: Chromium's M136 field trial showed decode-time regressions of +2% to +9% across percentiles on Android while desktop improved about 15% in total (discussion #562).

Windows builds where unfiltering dominates: issue #567 (Jan 2025) measured total decode time at 101% of libpng on Windows vs 79% on Linux, and 114-151% on one Paeth-heavy RGBA image, from different auto-vectorized code.
When you need libpng's full transform set (gamma correction, rgb-to-gray, background compositing, custom row callbacks): only EXPAND, STRIP_16 and ALPHA exist; colour handling is left to the caller.
Small-image workloads where the 2022 Wuffs numbers apply: on the 77k 8bpp paletted image png 0.17.5 was 0.89x libpng.

integration.dependencies: bitflags, crc32fast, fdeflate, flate2 (miniz_oxide backend by default; optional zlib-rs feature)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.81 (rust-version in Cargo.toml for 0.18.1); `unstable` feature needs nightly
integration.platforms: any Rust target; SIMD comes from compiler auto-vectorization at the target's baseline (SSE2 on x86-64 unless you raise target-cpu); wasm32 builds
integration.thread_safety: not documented beyond Rust's type system: each Decoder/Reader is a single-owner object; decode different images on different threads
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: replaces libpng's decode/encode role but with a different Rust API, no C ABI and fewer transforms

gotchas: Adler-32 is ignored by default (zlib.rs: `ignore_adler32: true`); call `Decoder::ignore_checksums(false)` or the StreamingDecoder setter if you need libpng-equivalent zlib integrity checking. Chunk CRCs are still verified.

Default output is the IDENTITY transform: paletted, low-bit-depth and 16-bit images come back in their stored layout unless you set EXPAND / STRIP_16 (`Transformations::normalize_to_color8()`); there is no BGRA or filler output.
0.18 changed the API: `Decoder` needs `BufRead + Seek`, `output_buffer_size()` returns `Option<usize>`, and the `Decoded` event enum was reworked; code written for 0.17 does not compile unchanged.
The nightly `unstable` (std::simd) feature can make decoding slower: Chromium disabled it after Windows regressions (issue #567), and the blog says it regresses ARM performance cores.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over libspng when you can host Rust: in the 2026 QOI-corpus run it decodes about 1.46x spng's geomean on the 7950X (339.9 vs 233.1 MP/s, derived), while libspng stays the C option. Pick it over zune-png for broader adoption, APNG, encoding and a slight decode lead in the same run (339.9 vs 313.2 MP/s), and over Wuffs when you want a conventional Rust crate rather than generated C (Wuffs' C decoder was 1.55x-3.16x libpng and faster than png 0.17.5 on every image in 2022).
verified_claims_summary: Third-party Wuffs mimic benchmark, September 2022: png 0.17.5 (Rust 1.48, `cargo --release`, miniz_oxide 0.5.3 inflate with Adler-32 and CRC checked) vs Debian Bullseye libpng 1.6.37 through the simplified API (harness built with gcc 10.2.1 / clang 11.0.1 -O3), decoding five test images to BGRA (gray stays gray) on an Intel Core i5-10210U: 1.53x, 1.77x, 0.89x, 1.03x and 1.23x libpng's MB/s. The Rust side's timed loop also includes a scalar RGB/RGBA-to-BGRA swizzle that libpng does internally, so the comparison slightly handicaps Rust; current 0.18.x has not been re-measured on that page.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-23, 0.18.1 current, about 245 million crates.io downloads), MIT OR Apache-2.0, shipped to all Chrome users since M139 (August 2025) and used by GNOME 49 through glycin; only one open bug-labelled issue (#286, zlib decompression may exceed allocation limits, 2021).
sources_read: WebSearch: Chromium Rust png crate SkPngRustCodec replace libpng performance (snippets only)
measurement_notes: Newer evidence beyond the catalogued Wuffs 2022 rows, for the orchestrator. (1) image-rs blog 2026-06-18 (first-party, author Shnatsel) with a public harness (fintelia/corpus-bench, branch png-0.18.0: png 0.18.0, fdeflate 0.3.7, image 0.25.8, libz-sys 1.1.22 with zlib-ng) on all 2,848 QOI-corpus images (gray+alpha images skipped): Ryzen 9 7950X geomean image-png 339.9, zune-png 313.2, wuffs-png 290.9, spng 233.1, libpng 180.4, stb_image 174.9 MP/s (image-png about 1.88x libpng, derived); Apple M4 310.5 vs libpng 177.6 (about 1.75x, derived). Measurement flaws in that harness: libpng (qoibench.c libpng_decode) is forced to 8-bit RGBA for every image (gray_to_rgb, filler alpha, strip_16) while image-png returns native layout (EXPAND only, 16-bit kept), so libpng writes more bytes per pixel; each image is decoded once with one Instant timing (no warm-up or repeats); the check closure always returns true, so outputs are not compared; libpng is a system static lib of unstated version and build flags; wuffs and spng closures include an extra image-crate header parse inside the timed region. Checksums: libpng is set to PNG_CRC_QUIET_USE, image-png verifies CRC but skips Adler-32, spng is set to IGNORE_ADLER32. These flaws favour image-png over libpng, so the blog ratio is an upper bound; it would be C (first-party) or at most B-like with caveats, and does not replace the A-tier Wuffs rows. (2) Chromium field data (discussion #562, M136 1% Stable trial): desktop PNG decode time summed over all samples improved about 15% (p25 +9% regression, p95/p99 about -16%), Android regressed about +9% overall. (3) Issue #567 (Chromium engineer, Jan 2025, 1,655-PNG top-500-sites corpus, 100 largest images): Rust/C++ total decode runtime 79% on Linux, 101% on Windows. No correctness bug found behind the catalogued Wuffs numbers: png 0.17.5 inflated with miniz_oxide 0.5.3, whose core.rs checks Adler-32 when TINFL_FLAG_PARSE_ZLIB_HEADER is set, and CRC32 was checked, so the 'verify_checksum' label holds; script/bench-rust-png has no Cargo.lock and pins png = "0.17" and rustc_version_runtime = "*", so a rerun today resolves png 0.17.16, not 0.17.5.
